lens: clarity & depth: would a curious 15-year-old follow it and an expert respect it; AlexNet and transformer step by step in sync; each era's belief, dissent, duration
summary: The two deep dives are the real thing. AlexNet (ch08, about 3.5 min) works a 3x3 edge stencil to real numbers (-4 clipped to 0, then 3.88), then covers depth, learned filters, ReLU, the 60M-weights vs 12M-bits overfitting problem, augmentation, dropout, the two-GPU split, the step-size schedule, the result and fair credit. The transformer (ch10, about 3.3 min) runs bottleneck, attention, Q/K/V, a dot-product example with correct softmax shares (0.20/0.07/0.53/0.20), the reason for dividing by the square root of d_k (8/0/-8 vs 1/0/-1), heads, position, blocks, parallelism, quadratic cost and the causal mask. The candle shelf gives nearly every era a stated belief, a named dissenter at its rim and an explicit duration (16, ~7, 17, ~7, 13, 10-15, 20, 39 years). The losses in clarity are mostly in pacing: a few foundational beats are crammed (pixels, position, dropout), real terms are rarely voiced, and the payoff line 'why choose the fog' plays over a static shelf instead of the bowl and fog it refers to. Depth is thinnest on classical ML and symbolic AI, which the brief names explicitly.

issues.problem: L0832 ('Why choose the fog? The rivals' clean bowl sat on stencils cut by hand. In the fog, given data and fire, the net cut its own...') is the thesis that ties classical ML to deep learning. It plays over the candle shelf and a small 'WHY WOULD ANYONE CHOOSE THE FOG?' card. Neither the bowl nor the fog appears, so a teenager hears an argument with no picture.
issues.fix: On the 'fogcard'/'bowl' beats (17.99-24.19), cut to the ch06-s03 clean bowl with a hand-cut tin stencil pinned under it (stamped 'by hand'). Then show the ch05-s05/ch08-s10 foggy hills with the learned stencil mosaic from ch08-s06 rising out of the fog on 'cut its own'. Hold each for at least 4 s, and keep the shelf only for L0826/L0831 and the 'newcandle' beat.

issues.problem: ch08-s03 ('A photograph is a grid of lights, each light a number') is the base of the whole AlexNet dive, and it gets 7.2 s at 227 wpm. The RGB planes, the 0.89 magnifier and '224 x 224 x 3 = 150,528' all appear in silence, so colour-as-three-numbers is never said.
issues.fix: Extend L0805: 'A photograph is a grid of lights, each light a number. In colour, three numbers: red, green, blue. One small photo: a hundred and fifty thousand numbers.' Re-time ch08-s03 to about 12 s, with the 'planes' beat on 'red, green, blue' and 'count' on 'hundred and fifty thousand'.

issues.problem: Positional encoding gets 7.7 s at 213 wpm. The shot's best insight is that after the shuffle the attention arcs come out the same, so attention is blind to order. That lasts about 1.5 s and is never narrated. 'Sines and cosines, fast to slow' appears only as a caption.
issues.fix: Re-time to about 14 s and split L1020: 'Shuffle the words, and attention can't tell: the scores come out the same. So each word wears a clock face set by its place in line, some hands fast, some slow.' Hold the shuffled state 2 s with the arc visibly unchanged, then land the clocks on 'clock face' and the fast/slow waves on 'fast, some slow'.

issues.problem: Dropout gets 8.6 s at 204 wpm, and the reason it helps (no lantern can rely on a neighbour, so knowledge spreads) passes in one clause. The 'dropout p = 0.5' label is the only place the real term appears.
issues.fix: Lengthen to about 12 s and extend L0830: '...so no lantern could count on another. Like a team where anyone might be missing, each had to know the work.' Hold two full snuff/relight cycles under the second sentence.

issues.problem: The metaphors are consistent and lovely: lanterns, knobs, messenger, fog, stencil, weir, jug, cards. But the real terms a curious viewer would search for afterwards are mostly never voiced: softmax, ReLU, dropout, overfitting, gradient descent, embedding, token. Experts also notice that 'each word arrives' hides tokenization.
issues.fix: After each metaphor's first use, name the trade term once with an on-screen label synced to the word (for example 'the jug of light, softmax to the trade'; 'the below-zero rule, ReLU'; 'downhill in fog, gradient descent'). Add a half-line in ch11-s02 that models read word-pieces (tokens), not whole words.

issues.problem: The brief names classical ML explicitly, but it gets one 24 s shot. Statistical speech/MT, forests and the SVM street fly past in about 10 s, and the kernel trick (bible: Boser, Guyon & Vapnik 1992) and the 'hand-made features + simple learner' recipe are never shown. Yet that recipe is exactly what AlexNet overturns (L0802, L0832).
issues.fix: Add a shot ch06-s03b (about 20-25 s) after ch06-s03: the classical recipe as a two-stage machine. An expert cuts the features by hand, a simple learner draws the line. Show the kernel trick as lifting the two crowds onto a hill so one flat cut separates them. Close on 'the learning was clean; the seeing was hand-made', which sets up L0802 and L0832.

issues.problem: The frog's-eye paper puts out the logic-machine candle, but the film never says why. 'Picking out features before the brain saw a thing' does not explain to a 15-year-old why that contradicts 'the brain is a logic machine'. The eye inset is also small and brief.
issues.fix: Using bible claim e1-frog, add the contrast: the eye was doing messy, local, analogue work (bug detectors, edge detectors), not clean all-or-nothing logic. Enlarge the eye inset to at least a third of the frame and hold it through the new clause.

issues.problem: The dissent from 'deep learning works on everything' is voiced anonymously. Adversarial-example and Gender Shades researchers are unnamed in narration (Buolamwini & Gebru only in small text). The best-known critic, Gary Marcus (2018 'Critical Appraisal', in the bible), appears only as an unvoiced quote card in ch11-s08. 'The candle burned on' gives no duration, unlike every other era.
issues.fix: Name them in L0910 ('...Joy Buolamwini and Timnit Gebru found commercial face software...'). Add a short line or name card for Marcus's 2018 appraisal at this rim, and close with a dated status ('lit 2012; still burning, still argued').

issues.problem: The export-control debate's dissenters appear only as small hanging tags in silence: 'DECISIVE' (Amodei, Khan), 'HELPS HUAWEI' (Huang), 'SELF-DEFEATING' (China's foreign ministry). The 'struck match, for a day' metaphor is hard for a teenager to decode.
issues.fix: Voice one even-handed sentence naming the three positions. Make the tags at least twice as large, each held 2 s. Gloss the match in plain words: 'for one day, investors bet that chips mattered less; the next weeks said otherwise' (or whatever the bible supports).

issues.problem: The first minute, the hook, runs fast despite 'very soft, unhurried' direction: L0102 229, L0103 217, L0109 248, L0114 249 wpm; ch01-s01 264, ch01-s06 249 per shot. A curious viewer has to lean in at exactly the moment the film needs to slow them down.
issues.fix: Re-narrate L0102-L0114 at about 150 wpm (slower ElevenLabs speed or added pauses), and let ch01-s02..s06 grow to fit. The clock will shift, so re-fit downstream shots and cues.

issues.problem: The unscaled example first shows scores '3 . 12 . -13', then silently swaps them to '8 . 0 . -8' before the pour. A careful viewer will think they missed a step.
issues.fix: Show only 8 . 0 . -8 from the start; or, if the first set is meant as 'scores swing wildly', narrate it and animate the swing explicitly before it settles.

issues.problem: A temperature dial and 'p = softmax(z/T)' are animated (the top share jumps 56% to 85% and back) with no narration. The beat raises a question it never answers.
issues.fix: Either drop the 'temperature' beat, or add a half-line to L1107: 'turn this dial and it grows bolder, or blander.'

issues.problem: 'In 2018, a Google team kept only the writing half' is correct (Liu et al., e10-liu-decoder), but OpenAI's GPT-1 (June 2018, e10-gpt1) goes unmentioned. Viewers then meet 'GPT-2' in L1103 with no idea where GPT came from, and experts will notice the gap.
issues.fix: Add an on-screen line on the 'cut' beat: 'Liu et al., Google, Jan 2018 · then OpenAI's GPT, June 2018'. Or extend L1032: '...kept only the writing half; months later OpenAI did the same, and called it GPT.'

issues.problem: Between L1025 and L1027, four dense facts appear on small cards in silence: 12 hours, one machine with 8 GPUs, about 1/7 the compute, 'EN to DE 27.3 to 28.4'. BLEU is unexplained and unreadable at speed.
issues.fix: Keep the sundial and '8 chips, half a day' (already in L1024's spirit), drop the BLEU numbers or move them to the honest-credit card, and give the silence at most two facts.

issues.problem: The honest-credit card ('not the first attention / not only attention / built to translate') types out in about 4 s of silence in small italic. This is the kind of nuance an expert respects, but most viewers will not finish reading it.
issues.fix: Hold the completed card at least 2.5 s longer, or voice it as a single short line: 'Not the first attention, nor attention alone; it was built to translate.'

issues.problem: Anthropic's founding (2021) is played as a flashback after ChatGPT (Nov 2022) and states only the self-description. Why former OpenAI researchers left to found a safety-branded lab, the 'what people believed' question for this era, goes unexplained.
issues.fix: If the bible supports it, add one sourced clause on the founders' stated reason. Otherwise move ch12-s03 before ch12-s06 so the chronology runs forward, and let L1207's self-description stand.

issues.problem: Under DEEP DIVE II, the densest explaining in the film, the m13 spectrogram shows sustained high energy from 20 to 200 Hz across almost the whole cue. Mix QA reports only 2.25 dB of ducking (target 3). Low-end bed under a male narrator's fundamentals during ch10-s05..s07 risks masking the numbers being read out.
issues.fix: High-pass the bed (about 150 Hz) and thin the texture under ch10-s05, s06 and s07, drop intensity under the worked-example lines L1011-L1017, and bring the duck to the 3 dB target.

issues.problem: By chapter 11 the candle shelf holds about 12 candles, each labelled in tiny vertical type. When the narrator names a candle ('the read-in-order candle', 'the fiddly-nets candle'), the viewer often cannot find it, and the shelf mechanic, the film's best clarity device, blurs.
issues.fix: Whenever a candle is named in narration, rotate its label horizontal and enlarge it next to the flame for about 2 s, with its date range, and dim the neighbouring candles.

best_moments: ch10-s06: a real attention computation a teenager can check by hand. Labels times bank's question give 2, 0, 4, 2; halved gives 1, 0, 2, 1; the jug pours 0.20/0.07/0.53/0.20 (correct softmax); bank then takes in 'water'. The jug lands exactly on 'Pour one jug of light'.

ch10-s07: why divide by sqrt(d_k), shown rather than asserted. 8/0/-8 tips everything into one cup ('learning freezes'), while 1/0/-1 pours 0.67/0.24/0.09 ('learning flows'), with the real formula underneath and a callback that our toy's 'halve' was the same sqrt(4).

ch08-s04: the pierced-tin stencil is a real vertical-edge kernel. A worked sum of -4 clips to 0, the next position gives 3.88 ('nearly four'), and sliding it everywhere lights the outline of the 4. Convolution earned, not named.

ch08-s08: the overfitting argument as a balance scale, 60,000,000 weights against 1.2 million labels x ~10 bits = 12 million. Then crops and mirrors pile onto the light pan. Expert-grade reasoning made physical.
ch04-s01: XOR with scissors. One cut always leaves a lantern on the wrong side (counter 1, 2, 1). Two cuts, the hidden layer, bring it to 0. The single cleanest 'aha' in the film.

ch02-s04 and the shelf device: each belief is a candle whose ruler ticks off the years it was held, with the dissenter (Ralph Gerard, dial vs switch) standing at the rim. It answers the brief's 'what people believed, who dissented, how long' structurally, era after era.
ch08-s13: the fair-credit beat (seven nets voting, one alone nearer 18%; a Swiss lab already winning on GPUs) is exactly the kind of honesty that earns an expert's respect.
ch08-s09: nobody told the two GPU halves how to divide the work, yet one learns edges and the other colour, every time, with the paper's own phrasing on cards.
ch15-s08: the case board turns into a neural network with one lantern still dark (interpretability). A closing image that leaves a question rather than an answer.
